tasks.text: Sure, I can help you design a geothermal heating and cooling system based on your demand profiles. Please provide me with the annual heating and cooling demand statistics (peaks, energy usage, seasonality), as well as any specific requirements or constraints that might influence the design.

The location of Delft is specified as 'Delft'. The reference year for this query is 2019. Therefore, I am fetching the ERA5 archive data from that year to set the cooling tower water temperatures for the simulations.

To make the design cheaper, we need to focus on reducing costs while maintaining feasibility. Let's start by analyzing the annual heating and cooling demand statistics (peaks, energy, seasonality) using `analyze_demand`. This will help us understand where the highest costs are incurred.

Once we have this information, we can proceed with designing a geothermal district heating/cooling system that balances cost efficiency with other constraints such as CO2 emissions. We'll use GEMINI's digital-twin physics tools to simulate and evaluate different designs based on our analysis of demand patterns

The LCOE of this design is EUR/MEUR 43.18 and the annual CO2 emissions are approximately 6190 t. This result was obtained using the fact ID F7, which describes a design with two doublets at a depth of 3100 m, an electric heat pump capacity of 10 MW, and a gas boiler capacity of 18 MW. The feasibility check passed.

The design with a geothermal share of heat at 99.15% and an LCOE of €43.18/MWh is cheaper per MWh compared to the one with a geothermal share of heat at 99.97% and an LCOE of €53.46/MWh, which emits less CO2 (5046 t/year vs 6190 t/year).

The design with the demand growth scenario is not feasible because it fails to meet cooling demand on all days of the year. Let's proceed without this design and focus on another one that meets the constraints.
